capitals.name: Jabal Masar (Haraz)
capitals.note: Ali's base; the coordinates are approximate (Manakhah).

capitals.name: Sana'a
capitals.note: 'Ali also controlled San'a since 1063'; the Ali page says he made it his capital.

rulers.name: Ali al-Sulayhi
rulers.note: Assassinated on the pilgrimage road; the Sulayhid page says 'the date is variously given as 1067 or 1081', the Zabid page has 1067.

rulers.name: al-Mukarram Ahmad
rulers.note: With Asma bint Shihab as co-ruler; 'ended in 1086 when he turned over governance to his wife Arwa'; died 1091 at Ashyah.

correction.text: the Haraz mountains round Jabal Masar and Manakhah, Ali al-Sulayhi's base

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1047-1061: the Haraz mountains. Page: 'In 1047 he gathered an armed force in Haraz and thus founded the Sulayhid dynasty (1047-1138)'; the Ali page: he 'began his revolt at Jabal Masur against the Zaydi rulers of Jabal Haraz' and repelled a Zaydi army of about 30,000. The page gives no area; a 50 km radius round Manakhah (not in the gazetteer) stands for the Haraz core. Sana'a followed only in 1063 and Zabid in 1062.

correction.text: most of historical Yemen at its peak: Tihama, the highlands and Aden, without the east (Hadramawt, Mahrah); years 1062-1065 only (1056-1061 is keyframe sulayhid-dynasty_1047, the Haraz core)

keyframe_review.note: 75,390 km2 for 1056-1065: the northern highlands (Sa'dah, Amran, Hajjah, Mahwit, part of Sana'a and of the Tihama) with Najran, Asir and Jizan. No page opened supports that shape. Pages: until 1061 the Sulayhid land was the Haraz core (new keyframe sulayhid-dynasty_1047); 'The first Sulayhid ruler conquered the whole of Yemen in 1062' (Sulayhid page; 'by 1063', Ali page), so 1062-1066 is the peak shape (new keyframe sulayhid-dynasty_1062), which the Sulayhid page describes as 'most of historical Yemen at its peak'. The page gives no area figure; the shape is under a third of Yemen's 528,000 km2.

correction.text: the whole of Yemen of 1062-1063 as the Sulayhid page has it ('conquered the whole of Yemen in 1062'), without Hadramawt and Mahrah

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1062-1066: Ali 'captured Zabid and the Tihamah "later in 1062"', 'conquered the rest of Yemen, including Aden, "by 1063"' and held Sana'a from 1063; the Hejaz and Mecca (1063-1064) are a client, not part of the shape (ledger vassal events). The Ali page does not mention Hadramawt, so the east is left out.

correction.text: the Sulayhid highlands (Sana'a, Haraz, Dhamar, Ibb) between the Najahid Tihama and the Zurayid coast; the Ibb highlands include Jibla, at-Ta'kar and Dhu Jibla; years 1067-1081, Zabid and the Tihama are Najahid

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1067-1081 (low confidence): after Ali's death (1066 on the Ali page, 1067 on the Zabid page) the Najahids held Zabid and the Tihama again (Zabid page: 'Sa'id Ibn Najah, the prince of Zabid' in 1067), the Zurayids ruled Aden from 1083 as tributaries, and Ahmad al-Mukarram ruled the highlands until 1086, then Arwa from Sana'a and, 'in about 1087', Jibla. The pages give no territorial extent for these years; the highland governorates are my reading of the places named (Sana'a, Haraz, al-Janad near Ta'izz, at-Ta'kar near Ibb). Saba' bin Ahmad fought the Najahids 'in the lowland' and died in 1098. Review fix: the first draft ran this shape to 1098; the Sulayhids recaptured Zabid and the Tihama in 1082 (next keyframe) and lost them again by 1089.

correction.text: the Sulayhid highlands of the 1067 keyframe plus Zabid and the Tihama (Al Hudaydah governorate), recaptured by al-Mukarram in 1082; years 1082-1088, the city contested from 1087

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1082-1088 (confidence 2 for the extent). Ali page: 'In 1082, al-Mukkaram led a Sulayhid force against Zabid, quickly capturing the city and Asma', forcing al-Ahwal to flee to the island of Dahlak, and 'reinstating Ibn Shihab as governor'. Najahid page: 'In 1087, Said al-Ahwal returned to Zabid but was killed that same year by Ahmed al-Mukkaram' (contest 1087-1089). The pages give no extent for the Sulayhid hold on the Tihama; Al Hudaydah governorate and an 80 km disc round Zabid are my reading, as in the 1062 gain. Review fix: the first draft typed 1082 as the start of a contest and kept the highlands-only shape for 1067-1098, although the page says the city was captured.

correction.text: the Sulayhid highlands (Sana'a, Haraz, Dhamar, Ibb) between the Najahid Tihama and the Zurayid coast; the Ibb highlands include Jibla, at-Ta'kar and Dhu Jibla; years 1089-1098, after the Najahids were back in Zabid

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1089-1098 (low confidence): the highlands again, with Zabid and the Tihama Najahid (Najahid page: Jayyash 1080-1089, Fatiq ibn Jayyash 1089-1104, 'Jayyash returned to Zabid disguised as an Indian', undated). Same extent as the 1067 keyframe, which has the same extent caveats; Saba' bin Ahmad fought the Najahids 'in the lowland' and died in 1098.

correction.text: Queen Arwa's Jibla, Dhu Jibla and at-Ta'kar in the Ibb highlands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1099-1138 (low confidence): after Saba' bin Ahmad's death in 1098 'San'a was lost' (the page does not say to whom; the infobox lists the Hamdanids of Sana'a among the successors), and Arwa ruled from Jibla; Ibn Najib ad-Dawla arrived in 1119 and failed in a coup in 1125; she died in 1138. The extent is the Ibb highlands round Jibla, at-Ta'kar and Dhu Jibla.

ledger.note: 1047: Ali al-Sulayhi founds the Sulayhid dynasty in the Haraz mountains. Page: 'In 1047 he gathered an armed force in Haraz and thus founded the Sulayhid dynasty (1047-1138)'; infobox 'Established 1047'. The page gives the mountains, not a boundary.

1062: the Sulayhids take Zabid and the Tihama from the Najahids. Page: his forces captured Zabid and the Tihamah 'later in 1062' (the Sulayhid page dates the poisoning of the Najahid ruler to 1060: 'poisoned in 1060 and his capital Zabid was taken by the Sulayhids').

region.text: Aden, ruled by the Banu Ma'n

ledger.note: 1062: Aden pays tribute. Page: 'The Ma'nids of Aden were defeated in 1062 and forced to pay tribute.' The Ali page has Aden conquered 'by 1063'.

region.text: Sana'a, which he made his capital

ledger.note: 1063: Sana'a comes under Ali's control. Page: 'Ali also controlled San'a since 1063, after bringing fighting against the Zaydiyyah to a successful conclusion.'

region.text: the whole of Yemen without Hadramawt and Mahrah

ledger.note: 1063: the rest of Yemen falls to Ali. Ali page: with Hamdani and Himyar support 'conquered the rest of Yemen, including Aden, "by 1063"'; the Sulayhid page: 'conquered the whole of Yemen in 1062, and proceeded northwards to occupy the Hejaz'. The page names no Yemeni rulers besides the Ma'nids and the Zaydis.

1064: Mecca takes a Sulayhid client king. Ali page: he 'moved into the Hejaz in late 1063 and conquered Mecca by 1064, installing a client king and having the Fatimid caliphs named in the khutba'; the Sulayhid page: 'For a time, the Sulayhids appointed the Emirs of Mecca'.

region.text: Zabid and the Tihamah, back under the Najahids

ledger.note: 1067: the Najahids are back in Zabid. Zabid page: 'In 1067, during the pilgrimage to Mecca, the Banu Najah clan under Sa'id Ibn Najah, the prince of Zabid,' attacked and killed Ali al-Sulayhi (the Ali page has 1066 and the Najahid page no year); Asma was taken and 'her son stormed Zabid and freed her' (undated). The page does not date the Sulayhid loss of the Tihama; 1067 is the first year the Najahids hold Zabid.
1067: Sulayhid influence at Mecca ends with Ali's death. Page silent: the Sulayhid page says only 'for a time'; the end is inferred from Ali's death on the pilgrimage road.

region.text: Zabid and the Tihama, with the town of Asma

ledger.note: 1082: al-Mukarram recaptures Zabid. Ali page: 'In 1082, al-Mukkaram led a Sulayhid force against Zabid, quickly capturing the city and Asma', forcing al-Ahwal to flee to the island of Dahlak, and 'reinstating Ibn Shihab as governor'. Review fix: the first draft typed this a contest_start.
1083: the Zurayid brothers are set over Aden. Zurayids page: 'The brothers were placed in power in 1083'; the Sulayhid page: they 'came to power in 1083, at first as Sulayhid tributaries'.

1083: the Ma'nid tributary at Aden is replaced by the Zurayids. Page: the Ma'nids ruled Aden from before 1062 and the Zurayid brothers were 'placed in power in 1083'; the end of Ma'nid rule is the page's implication, not a stated date.

1087: Queen Arwa moves the capital from Sana'a to Jibla. Page: 'She established her capital in Jibla rather than Sana'a in about 1087.' Ahmad al-Mukarram's reign ended in 1086 'when he turned over governance to his wife Arwa'.

1087: the Najahids come back to Zabid. Najahid page: 'In 1087, Said al-Ahwal returned to Zabid but was killed that same year by Ahmed al-Mukkaram.' Whether the Sulayhids held the city after his death is not on the page; the contest runs to 1089.

1089: the Najahids hold Zabid again. Najahid page: 'Jayyash returned to Zabid disguised as an Indian' (undated) and his reign is listed 1080-1089, Fatiq ibn Jayyash 1089-1104. The page gives no year for the return; 1089 is the latest year it allows.

region.text: Zabid and the Tihama, back under the Najahids

ledger.note: By 1089 the Sulayhids no longer hold Zabid: Jayyash's undated return (Najahid page) and Fatiq's accession in 1089. Confidence 1: the page is silent on the year and on whether the Tihama went with the city.

1098: Sana'a is lost. Page: Saba' bin Ahmad 'fought vigorously against the Najahids in the lowland and died in 1098. After his demise San'a was lost to the Sulayhids' (sic). Page silent on the new holder and the year; the infobox names the Hamdanids of Yemen among the successors.

1110: Aden slips out of Sulayhid tutelage. Zurayids page: the brothers died at the siege of Zabid in the Sulayhid campaign of 1110 and 'After 1110 the Zurayids thus led a more than 60 years long independent rule in the city'.

region.text: the Ibb highlands with Jibla, Dhu Jibla and at-Ta'kar, where Arwa's last seat stood

ledger.note: 1138: Queen Arwa dies and the Sulayhid dynasty ends. Page: 'With her death in 1138, there was no-one left of the dynasty, and the Sulayhid era came to an end.' Infobox successors: the Zurayids, Hamdanids of Yemen, Najahids and Sulaymanids; the Zurayid page gives Muhammad bin Saba (1139-1153) Dhu Jibla, at-Ta'kar, Ibb and Habb 'after marrying the last Sulayhid queen'.

wars.name: Sulayhid conquest of Yemen
wars.outcome: Ali al-Sulayhi rose in Haraz in 1047, took Zabid and the Tihama in 1062, forced Aden to pay tribute (1062) and held Sana'a from 1063, 'conquered the whole of Yemen in 1062' on the Sulayhid page.
wars.note: Ali page: Najah poisoned in 1060, Zabid taken later in 1062, the rest of Yemen 'by 1063'.

wars.name: Sulayhid campaign in the Hejaz
wars.outcome: Ali moved into the Hejaz in late 1063, took Mecca by 1064, installed a client king and had the Fatimids named in the khutba.

wars.name: Sulayhid-Najahid wars
wars.outcome: The Najahids killed Ali on the pilgrimage road (1066 or 1067) and held Zabid; al-Mukarram captured Zabid and Asma in 1082 and al-Ahwal fled to Dahlak; Said al-Ahwal returned to Zabid in 1087 and was killed the same year by al-Mukarram; Jayyash returned to Zabid (undated) and the Najahids held it by 1089.
wars.note: Zabid page: the attack on Ali is dated 1067; Najahid page gives no year for the Najahid return before 1087. Review fix: the first draft said al-Mukarram 'marched on Zabid in 1082 ... without taking the city'; the Ali page says he captured it.

wars.name: Sulayhid campaign against Zabid (1110)
wars.outcome: The Sulayhid leader al-Mufaddal besieged Zabid with the Zurayid brothers, who were both killed in the siege; the city held.

certainty.note: No boundary line appears on the pages opened; the highlands, the Tihama and Aden are named places, and the peak extent is 'most of historical Yemen'.

notes:
Pages: the Sulayhid dynasty and Ali al-Sulayhi (budget 1-2), plus the Najahid, Zabid and Zurayids pages opened for the neighbours and cited here for the Sulayhid-Najahid and Aden events.
Cliopatria holds one Sulayhid shape, 1056-1065 (75,390 km2, the northern highlands with Sa'dah, Najran and Asir); the dynasty ran 1047-1138 on the page. The shape is marked wrong; the dossier carries six new keyframes (1047 Haraz core, 1062 whole Yemen, 1067 highlands, 1082 highlands with Zabid and the Tihama, 1089 highlands, 1099 Ibb highlands). The 1067, 1089 and 1099 keyframes are low confidence: no page opened gives their extent. Cliopatria's Najahid row from 1066 is an all-Yemen union (see najahid-dynasty) and its Ziyadid row to 1138 overlaps the same land.
Pages disagree: Najah's poisoning 1060 (Sulayhid page) but Zabid captured 'later in 1062' (Ali page); Ali killed 1066 (Ali page), 1067 (Zabid page) or 1081 (variants on the Sulayhid page); Hejaz late 1063 and Mecca by 1064 (Ali page) against 'conquered the whole of Yemen in 1062, and proceeded northwards to occupy the Hejaz' (Sulayhid page). Najahids held Zabid in 1067 although the Ali page has the Sulayhids holding it from 1062: the date of the Najahid return is not on any page.
The Fatimid allegiance ('The regime was confederate with the Cairo-based Fatimid Caliphate'; Ali 'shifted Yemen's allegiance from the Abbasids' in 1062) is not territory; the Fatimid dossier may record it.
Cross-check with the Fatimid dossier on the mount (read by grep): it dates the Fatimid da'i Ali al-Sulayhi's capture of San'a to 1048 and a campaign 'to conquer all of Yemen, capturing Aden and Zabid' to 1060, from another page; the Sulayhid and Ali pages used here put Sana'a in 1063 and Zabid in 1062. The Fatimid dossier carries the Sulayhid tie as a vassal tint to 1138; this dossier does not repeat it.
Counterparts without a dossier: rassids (Zaydi imamate of Sa'dah and Haraz), hamdanids-of-sanaa, sharifate-of-mecca, the Ma'nids of Aden, the Sulaymanids (infobox successor, not opened).
Gazetteer names needed: Manakhah / Jabal Haraz (a 50 km radius at 43.75 E, 15.07 N is used), Jibla, Dhu Jibla, at-Ta'kar.
Review repair (2026-10-20): the Ali page (re-opened) says 'In 1082, al-Mukkaram led a Sulayhid force against Zabid, quickly capturing the city and Asma', so 1082 is now a gain of Zabid and the Tihama from the Najahids (confidence 3) with a keyframe 1082-1088; the Najahid page has Said al-Ahwal back in Zabid in 1087 (killed that year) and Jayyash returning 'disguised as an Indian' (undated; Jayyash 1080-1089, Fatiq 1089-1104), so 1087-1089 is a contest and the Tihama is a loss at 1089 (confidence 1). The 1056 Cliopatria shape is now corrected for 1062-1065 only. Still thin: what the Sulayhids held between the 1062-1066 peak and the 1067 highlands (Sa'dah, Hajjah, Amran, al-Jawf, Ma'rib, al-Bayda, Shabwah, Abyan, Taiz, Aden-Lahij leave with no event except the Tihama and Aden's 1083 tribute), who took Sana'a after 1098, and the end of the Mecca tutelage (pages not re-opened: Arwa al-Sulayhi, Hamdanid sultans of Yemen, Sharif of Mecca).
